**Hello, I’m [Your Name], a clinician who specializes in postpartum mental health.**  

I’d like to invite you to complete the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)** today. This short, ten‑item questionnaire helps us understand how you’ve been feeling over the past week and lets us identify any signs of postpartum depression or anxiety so we can provide the support you deserve.

Everything you share is completely confidential, and this is a safe, non‑judgmental space. My goal is simply to listen and learn about your experience as a new mother.

The EPDS consists of ten conversational questions. I’ll ask them one at a time, and you can answer in whatever words feel most honest to you. If at any point you feel uncomfortable or have questions, please let me know.

Whenever you’re ready, we can begin.

**First question:**  
*In the past seven days, how often have you felt unable to enjoy things that you used to look forward to?*

I’ve noticed that a few things that I used to look forward to don’t feel quite the same. I still enjoy some moments with my baby and a few small things, but overall I’ve been feeling less excitement about the things I used to love. It’s not all the time, but it’s happening more often than before—maybe a few days out of the week.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

These days I can still laugh and see the funny side of things sometimes, especially when I’m with my baby or when something light happens. But it’s not as frequent as it used to be—I’d say I manage to feel that way only a few times in the past week, maybe two or three days.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do still look forward to a few things—especially moments with my baby, a short walk, or a quiet cup of tea—but it’s not as often as it used to be. Some days I feel that little spark of excitement, and other days I just go through the motions without really feeling the enjoyment. Overall, I’d say I’ve been able to look forward to things on a few days this past week, maybe two or three, but many days it’s harder to feel that same anticipation.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes, I’ve found myself blaming myself a bit when something doesn’t go as planned—like if I’m late with a feeding or if I feel like I’m not soothing my baby enough. It happens occasionally, but it’s not a constant feeling; most of the time I can remind myself that I’m doing my best.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I’ve felt anxious or worried for no clear reason a few times this past week—maybe on two or three days. Most of those worries are about my baby’s health or whether I’m doing enough, and they usually settle down fairly quickly once I take a breath and remind myself I’m doing my best.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

There have been a couple of moments this past week where I felt a sudden surge of fear or panic that didn’t seem to match the situation—maybe when I heard a strange noise at night or when I was trying to get my baby to settle and it just didn’t work right away. It was brief, and after a few minutes I was able to calm down, but those spikes have happened on a few occasions, probably two or three times in the last seven days.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, there have been moments this week when everything just feels a little too much. I’m juggling feedings, sleep, and trying to keep the house in order, and on a few days it feels like the little tasks start to pile up and weigh on me. It’s not constant, but when it happens I notice I get more irritable and a bit overwhelmed, though I usually manage to take a short break, breathe, and keep going. I’d say it’s been happening on a couple of days in the past week.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I’ve been feeling a bit down at times, and on a couple of nights it’s made it harder for me to fall asleep. It’s not that I can’t sleep at all—I still get a decent amount of rest overall—but those evenings when I’m especially unhappy, I lie awake a little longer before I finally drift off. It’s only happened on a few nights in the past week.
I have felt sad or miserable

I’ve felt sad or a bit miserable on a few days this past week—maybe three or four days. It’s usually a low mood that comes when I’m exhausted or when something doesn’t go as smoothly as I hoped, but it isn’t overwhelming and it lifts fairly quickly.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes, there have been a couple of times this week when I felt really down and ended up crying. One evening after a particularly stressful feeding, I just broke down and cried for a few minutes, and then another night when I was feeling overwhelmed by everything, I had another short crying spell. It’s not happening all the time, but those moments have been pretty noticeable.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts of harming myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 14: **Postpartum Mood & Anxiety Screening – Summary**

**Client Identifiers:**  
- Post‑partum mother (time since delivery not specified)  
- Completed 10‑item screening questionnaire

---

### 1. Reported Symptoms & Emotional/Behavioral Concerns
| Item | Symptom / Concern | Frequency (per week) |
|------|-------------------|----------------------|
| Q1 – Laughter / humor | Ability to laugh, see funny side – present only “a few times” | 2‑3 days |
| Q2 – Anticipation / enjoyment | Looks forward to some activities (baby, walks, tea) – limited | 2‑3 days |
| Q3 – Self‑blame | Occasional unnecessary self‑blame for parenting lapses | intermittent |
| Q4 – Unexplained anxiety/worry | Anxiety about baby’s health, adequacy of care – brief episodes | 2‑3 days |
| Q5 – Fear / panic spikes | Sudden, brief panic/fear (e.g., strange noises) | 2‑3 episodes |
| Q6 – Feeling overwhelmed | “Things getting on top of me,” irritability, need for short breaks | 2 days |
| Q7 – Mood‑related sleep difficulty | Trouble falling asleep on “a couple of nights” when unhappy | 2 nights |
| Q8 – Sadness / misery | Low mood on 3‑4 days, generally linked to exhaustion or setbacks | 3‑4 days |
| Q9 – Crying spells | Two distinct crying episodes (stressful feeding, overall overwhelm) | 2 episodes |
| Q10 – Suicidal ideation | No thoughts of self‑harm | None |

---

### 2. Consistent Patterns Across Responses
- **Low mood / anhedonia:** Reduced frequency of laughter and anticipation; sadness on multiple days.  
- **Anxiety & worry:** Recurrent, brief anxiety/panic episodes focused on infant’s wellbeing and personal performance.  
- **Guilt/self‑blame:** Intermittent but present feelings of unnecessary self‑criticism.  
- **Overwhelm & irritability:** Reports of tasks feeling “on top of me” on several days.  
- **Sleep impact:** Mood‑linked difficulty initiating sleep on a few nights.  
- **Crying:** Noticeable emotional release (2 episodes) in response to stress.

---

### 3. Areas of Screening Significance (Post‑partum Depression / Anxiety)
- **Anhedonia / loss of pleasure** (Q1, Q2)  
- **Persistent sadness / low mood** (Q8)  
- **Crying spells** (Q9)  
- **Sleep disturbance related to mood** (Q7)  
- **Excessive guilt / self‑blame** (Q3)  
- **Generalized anxiety, worry, panic symptoms** (Q4, Q5)  
- **Perceived inability to cope / feeling overwhelmed** (Q6)  
- **Absence of suicidal ideation** (Q10) – safety check completed.

---

### 4. Highlighted Risk Factors
- **Emotional distress:** Frequent low mood, reduced enjoyment, and crying episodes suggest moderate depressive symptomatology.  
- **Anxiety/panic:** Recurrent unexplained worry and brief panic spikes indicate anxiety component.  
- **Sleep disruption:** Mood‑related insomnia on multiple nights may exacerbate mood and anxiety.  
- **Self‑critical thoughts:** Occasional unnecessary self‑blame may contribute to feelings of worthlessness.  
- **Safety:** No suicidal thoughts reported; no immediate self‑harm risk identified at this time.

---

### 5. Screening Observation Summary
The client reports a pattern of reduced positive affect (limited laughter and anticipation), intermittent low mood, occasional crying, and brief anxiety/panic episodes over the past week. Sleep initiation difficulties appear linked to moments of heightened unhappiness. Self‑blame is present but not pervasive. No suicidal ideation is reported. These findings are consistent with moderate symptom burden for postpartum depression and anxiety, warranting continued monitoring and further comprehensive assessment. No acute safety concerns are identified at this time.
